Present claim petition has been filed by the petitioners being legal heirs of deceased Rajpal Singh s/o Partap Singh.
Facts in brief are that on 27.05.2016 at about 04.00 a.m. after loading dust in buffalo cart, deceased Rajpal Singh was going to Siyana.

When deceased reached near PIC Inter College, Kasba Siyana, in the meanwhile a Canter bearing no.UP-80BT-8940 being driven by its driver/respondent no.1 at very high speed, rashly, negligently and violating traffic rules came from front side and hit the buffalo cart of the deceased.
As a result of such impact, deceased fell down on the road and sustained fatal injuries and diet at the spot.
It is stated that respondent no.1 is the driver of the offending vehicle and it was owned by respondent no.2.
However the said vehicle was not insured.

Regarding the accident in question an FIR No.166/2016 of PS Siyana, District Bulandshahr, UP was registered u/s 279/427/304A IPC.
2.
Upon filing of claim petition, its notice was issued to the respondents.
However despite service of notice respondents did not appear in the court and thus were proceeded exparte on 08.02.2019.

3. Since respondents did not appear before this Tribunal and Digitally signed by SHAILENDER MACT No.263/2017 SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date: Page 2 2024.02.16 12:26:25 +0530 were proceeded exparte, matter was straightway fixed for petitioner evidence.

However for proper adjudication of the matter, following issue is being framed :
"Whether deceased died due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle bearing no.UP-80BT-8940 on 27.05.2016 being driven by respondent no.1?"
4.
In order to substantiate their case petitioners have examined two witnesses.
PW1 is Smt.Suraj (widow of deceased) and PW2 Manoj stated to be an eye witness of the accident.
5. I have heard Sh.Yogendre Kumar, ld. counsel for petitioner.
I have gone through written submissions filed on behalf of petitioner and entire material available on record.
6. It is settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the claim petition based upon negligence.

Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Suraj vs Sadim on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198215237/

7. PW1 Smt.Suraj though deposed in her deposition regarding the occurrence of accident, however it is matter of record that she was not SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date:

8. Petitioners have also examined PW2 Manoj s/o Champat who deposed that he is eye witness in this case and well conversant with the facts and circumstances.
PW2 deposed that on 27.05.2016 he and Rajpal Singh were going to Siyana from Bahadurgarh after loading dust in their buffalo cart.

PW2 testified that at about 4.00 a.m. when they reached near Public Inter College, Kasba Siyana, in the meanwhile a Canter bearing registration no.UP-80BT-8940 being driven by its driver at very high speed, rashly and negligently came from opposite side and after changing its driving lane hit the buffalo cart of Rajpal Singh with a great force.
PW2 states that as a result of such impact, Rajpal Singh sustained fatal injuries and died on the spot.
Thereafter his post mortem was conducted at mortuary, Bulandshahr, UP.
PW2 deposed that accident took place due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of Canter no.UP-80BT-8940 and police recorded his statement regarding the accident.
9. PW2 was not cross-examined at all as both the respondents remained exparte and no one appeared on their behalf to cross examine this witness.
Thus testimony of PW2 being eye witness of the accident remained unrebutted, unchallenged and uncontroverted.
Moreover testimony of PW2 has been corroborated from police documents Ex.PW1/10.

Perusal of certified copy of criminal case record Ex.PW1/10 shows that respondent no.1/driver was charge sheeted by the police of UP in criminal case being FIR No.166/2016 of PS Siyana, District Bulandshahr, UP for causing accident while driving offending vehicle bearing no.UP-80BT-8940.

Site plan of the place of accident, DL of respondent no.1, RC of offending vehicle and post mortem report of deceased are also on record Mechanical inspection report of the said MACT No.263/2017 by SHAILENDER SHAILENDER MALIK Page 4 MALIK Date: 2024.02.16 12:26:43 +0530 offending vehicle is also on record.

10. Testimony of PW2 who is eye witness to the accident in question coupled with record of criminal case in the opinion of this Tribunal is sufficient to establish that deceased died due to rash and negligent driving of offending car bearing registration no.UP-80BT-8940 being driven by respondent no.1.
11.

sentences.text: As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.

A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v.
Willoughby (1970) Ac 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid).
COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION 12.
The present case pertains to the death of deceased Rajpal Singh.

In death cases, the guidelines for computation of compensation have been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121.

sentences.text: The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balanc expired e which is considered to be the contribution to the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Step-2 (Ascertaining the multiplier)
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.

Having regard to several imponderables in Digitally signed by SHAILENDER MACT No.263/2017 Page 6 SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date:
2024.02.16 12:26:57 +0530 life and economic factors, a table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
The multiplier should be chosen from the said table with reference to the age of the deceased.
Step-3 (Actual Calculation)

The annual contribution to the family(multiplicand)
when multiplied by such multiplier gives the 'loss of dependency' to the family.
Thereafter, a conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000/- to Rs.10,000/- may be added as loss of estates.
Where the deceased is survived by his widow, another conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000 to Rs.10,000 should be added under the head of loss of consortium.
But no amount is to be awarded under the head of pain, suffering or hardship caused to the legal heirs of the deceased.

The funeral expenses, cost of transportation of the body (if incurred) and the cost of any medical treatment of the deceased before death (if incurred) should also be added."

PECUNIARY DAMAGES:
Age of deceased :
14.
The petitioner no.1 Smt.Suraj (PW1) in her evidence has proved copy of Aadhar card of deceased Rajpal Singh as Ex.PW1/1 wherein date of birth of deceased is mentioned as 01.01.1981.
As per this document Ex.PW1/1, age of deceased on the date of his death is 35 years.
There is nothing contrary on the record from the side of respondents regarding age of deceased.
This document in the opinion of this Tribunal is conclusive proof of age of deceased.
Thus, age of deceased as on the date of accident (27.05.2016) was 35 years.

15.
Petitioner no.1 (PW1) in her deposition stated that her deceased husband was working as a labour and was getting salary of Rs.12,000/- per month.
As per copy of Aadhar card of deceased Ex.PW1/1, he was resident of UP.
It is also matter of record that accident in question took place in UP.
However it is matter of record that no documentary evidence has been placed on record by the petitioners to prove the work and income of the deceased.

In the absence of any documentary evidence and material, this Tribunal is of the view that petitioners have failed to prove that deceased was working as a labourer or that he used to earn Rs.12,000/- per month at the time of his death.

In the absence of any such material this Tribunal income of deceased is taken to be at parity with minimum wages of unskilled worker in the State of U.P. which at the time of accident was of Rs.7,107.64 per month.

Application of Multiplier:
16.
As held above, deceased was 35 years of age at the time of accident.
An appropriate multiplier has to be determined for computation of compensation.
The judgment titled as Sarla Verma v. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121 is relevant to consider the multiplier.
In Para 21 of the judgment, the guidelines for the multiplier were laid down in accordance with age are as under:

MULTIPLIER AGE GROUP OF DECEASED  M-18 Age group between 15 to 20 & 21  to 25 years)
 M-17 Age group between 26 to 30 yrs  M-16 Age group between 31 to 35 yrs  M-15 Age group between 36 to 40 yrs  SHAILENDER MALIK
M-14 Age group between 41 to 45 yrs
M-13 Age group between 46 to 50 yrs  M-11 Age group between 51 to 55 yrs  M-9 Age group between 56 to 60 yrs  M-7 Age group between 61 to 65 yrs  M-5 Age group between 66 and above 17.
In view of the above, multiplier of 16 has to be applied against the age bracket of 31 to 35 years to determine the compensation.

Deduction towards Personal Living Expenses:
20. After choosing the age, multiplier and income of the deceased, necessary deductions have to be made out of the income of the deceased towards his personal expenses.

Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Reshma Kumari & Ors. v. Madan Mohan & Anr., (2013) 9 SCC 65, in para 30, laid down the necessary deductions towards personal living and expenses of deceased as under :
Deductions out of earning of the Number of deceased dependents Where dependent is 1 Half Where the number of dependent family 1/3rd members is 2 to 3 Where the number of dependent family 1/4th members is 4 to 6 Where the number of dependent family 1/5th members exceeds 6 (six)

In the absence of any documentary evidence and material, this Tribunal is of the view that petitioners have failed to prove that deceased was working as a labourer or that he used to earn Rs.12,000/- per month at the time of his death.
In the absence of any such material this Tribunal income of deceased is taken to be at parity with minimum wages of unskilled worker in the State of U.P. which at the time of accident was of Rs.7,107.64 per month.
Application of Multiplier:
16.
An appropriate multiplier has to be determined for computation of compensation.
Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Reshma Kumari & Ors. v. Madan Mohan & Anr., (2013) 9 SCC 65, in para 30, laid down the necessary deductions towards personal living and expenses of deceased as under :
Deductions out of earning of the Number of deceased dependents Where dependent is 1 Half Where the number of dependent family 1/3rd members is 2 to 3 Where the number of dependent family 1/4th members is 4 to 6 Where the number of dependent family 1/5th members exceeds 6 (six)

Instant claim petition has been filed by eight petitioners i.e. widow of deceased and minor children of deceased.
Since, the deceased was survived by eight dependents, one-fifth of the income of the deceased is to be deducted towards his personal living expenses.
NON-PECUNIARY DAMAGES:
22.
In case of Pranay Sethi (Supra), a compensation of Rs.40,000/-, 15,000/- and Rs.15,000/-
respectively has been fixed on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses.
Therefore, a compensation of Rs.40,000/-, 15,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses is required to be granted and further, it is required to be enhanced @ 10% in every three years.
Therefore, a compensation of Rs.48,000/-,
18,000/- and Rs.18,000/- respectively on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses is required to be granted.
Further, in view of recent decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case titled as United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur & Ors., Civil Appeal no. 2705 of 2020, decided on 30.06.2020, loss of consortium has to be fixed for each of the LRs.
Since, the deceased was survived by eight legal heirs, therefore, the claimants are entitled to a sum of Rs.4,20,000/- (48,000 X 8 + 18,000 + 18,000) under this head.
